def-discrete-convolutional-layer:
## Definition

Let $D,O\subseteq\mathbb Z^2$ be input and output index sets, let $C_{\rm in},C_{\rm out}$ be positive integers, and let $x:D\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ assign a row vector of input channels to each input site. A boundary extension is a function $\widetilde x:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ whose restriction to $D$ is $x$; zero padding is the extension that is zero off $D$. Choose a finite receptive-field offset set $K\subseteq\mathbb Z^2$, a positive integer stride vector $s\in\mathbb Z_{>0}^2$, an origin $a\in\mathbb Z^2$, one matrix $W_\delta\in\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}\times C_{\rm out}}$ for each $\delta\in K$, and an output bias row vector $b\in\mathbb R^{C_{\rm out}}$. The discrete convolutional layer is the map $y:O\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm out}}$ given by

$$
y(p)=b+\sum_{\delta\in K}\widetilde x(a+s\odot p+\delta)W_\delta\qquad(p\in O),
$$

where $s\odot p$ is coordinatewise multiplication. Thus each output uses only the input sites in its receptive field, mixes input channels by matrix multiplication, and uses the same weights and bias at every output site. With unit stride on the full lattice and no boundary truncation, this formula is a discrete cross-correlation; many machine-learning software packages call it convolution. Mathematical convolution instead reverses the kernel offsets. The choices of $O$, the extension $\widetilde x$, and the stride specify cropping, padding, and subsampling, and need not preserve a symmetry of the full lattice.
def-group-action-on-feature-maps:
## Definition

Let $G$ be a group acting on the left on a set $S$, and let $V$ be a set of feature values. A feature map is a function $f:S\to V$. For $u\in G$, the induced transformation of feature maps is

$$
(L_u f)(x)=f(u^{-1}\cdot x)\qquad(x\in S).
$$

It is a left action on the set of feature maps: the group acts by reindexing sites and leaves the feature values unchanged. In particular, for maps $F:G\to V$ on the group itself with its left multiplication action, $(L_uF)(g)=F(u^{-1}g)$.
def-p4-p4m-lattice-symmetry-groups:
## Definition

Let $\rho=\begin{pmatrix}0&-1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}$ be the quarter-turn matrix and $\sigma=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$ a reflection matrix. Let $C_4=\{\rho^j:j=0,1,2,3\}$ and $D_4=\{\rho^j,\rho^j\sigma:j=0,1,2,3\}$, with matrix multiplication. For $A=C_4$ or $D_4$, define $P_A=\mathbb Z^2\times A$ with multiplication

$$
(t,M)(s,N)=(t+Ms,MN).
$$

Each pair $(t,M)$ acts on lattice sites by $x\mapsto Mx+t$. The p4 lattice-symmetry group is $P_{C_4}$, generated by integer translations and quarter-turns. The p4m lattice-symmetry group is $P_{D_4}$, generated by integer translations, quarter-turns, and reflections. Their orientation subgroups have respectively four and eight elements, but both full groups are infinite because they contain every integer translation.
def-equivariant-neural-layer:
## Definition

Let a group $G$ act on sets $X$ and $Y$ by left actions $T$ and $T'$, respectively. A layer is a function $\Phi:X\to Y$. It is $G$-equivariant when

$$
\Phi(T_gx)=T'_g\Phi(x)\qquad(g\in G,\ x\in X).
$$

The input and output actions need not be the same. The layer is $G$-invariant when the output action $T'_g$ is the identity on $Y$ for every $g\in G$.
def-group-convolution:
## Definition

Let $G$ be a discrete group acting on the lattice $\mathbb Z^2$ on the left. Let $C_{\rm in},C_{\rm out}$ be positive integers, and regard channel vectors as row vectors. For a feature map $f:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ and a filter $\Psi:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}\times C_{\rm out}}$, the group-to-group cross-correlation is the map $C_\Psi f:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm out}}$ defined by

$$
(C_\Psi f)(g)=\sum_{h\in G} f(h)\Psi(g^{-1}h).
$$

For an image feature map $f:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ and a lattice filter $\Psi:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}\times C_{\rm out}}$, the first-layer image-to-group cross-correlation is the map $E_\Psi f:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm out}}$ defined by

$$
(E_\Psi f)(g)=\sum_{x\in\mathbb Z^2} f(x)\Psi(g^{-1}\cdot x).
$$

Each displayed sum is required to have finite support or to converge absolutely in every output coordinate. The first operation takes group-indexed features and filters; the second takes lattice-indexed image features and filters and returns group-indexed features. These are cross-correlations, with the filter argument displayed as written; they need not be commutative, and no finiteness of $G$ is assumed.
def-pointwise-nonlinearity-and-pooling-o:
## Definition

Let $G$ be a group and let $F:G\to\mathbb R^C$ be a feature map with $C$ channels. A pointwise nonlinearity determined by $\nu:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is $N_\nu F$, where $(N_\nu F)(g)_c=\nu(F(g)_c)$. For a nonempty finite set $U\subseteq G$, non-strided neighborhood max pooling is $P_UF$, where $(P_UF)(g)_c=\max_{u\in U}F(gu)_c$; the output is still indexed by $G$. For a subgroup $H\le G$, subgroup sampling is the restriction $R_HF=F|_H$, indexed by $H$.

The right-coset set is $G/H=\{gH:g\in G\}$, where $gH=\{gh:h\in H\}$. Its left $G$-action is $a\cdot(gH)=(ag)H$. For finite $H$, right-coset max pooling is the map $Q_HF:G/H\to\mathbb R^C$ given by $(Q_HF)(gH)_c=\max_{h\in H}F(gh)_c$. All maxima are taken separately in each channel. When $H=G$ is finite, $G/H$ has one element and $Q_HF$ is a group-invariant summary.
thm-group-convolution-equivariance:
## Statement

Let $G$ be a discrete group acting on the left on the square lattice $\mathbb Z^2$, and let feature maps take values in finite-dimensional row-vector channel spaces. Assume every group or lattice sum below has finite support or converges absolutely in each output coordinate. For group-indexed features $f:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ and a matrix-valued filter $\Psi:G\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}\times C_{\rm out}}$, group-to-group cross-correlation satisfies

$$
C_\Psi(L_u f)=L_u(C_\Psi f)\qquad(u\in G).
$$

For an image feature map $f:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}}$ and a lattice filter $\Psi:\mathbb Z^2\to\mathbb R^{C_{\rm in}\times C_{\rm out}}$, the first-layer image-to-group cross-correlation also satisfies

$$
E_\Psi(L_u f)=L_u(E_\Psi f)\qquad(u\in G),
$$

where the input action is induced by the action on $\mathbb Z^2$ and the output action is the left action on maps on $G$. The ordinary full-lattice, unit-stride discrete cross-correlation is the translation-group instance of this formula. Componentwise pointwise nonlinearities and finite-neighborhood max pooling without subsampling commute with the left action. Restricting a group feature map to a subgroup $H\le G$ preserves $H$-equivariance; finite right-coset max pooling produces a $G$-equivariant feature map on $G/H$, and when $H=G$ is finite it is invariant. Finite compositions of equivariant layers remain equivariant.

The full p4 and p4m lattice symmetry groups are infinite because they contain all integer translations; no finiteness assumption on $G$ is made. On a finite grid, the theorem applies only when the domain, output sampling, and boundary convention respect the stated actions. Arbitrary cropping, padding, or stride need not do so. No continuous-rotation, universal-approximation, or empirical-superiority claim follows.
